examples.ko: 요즘 고강도 운동을 해서 몸이 너무 아파요.
examples.en: I've been doing high-intensity workouts lately, so my body aches a lot.
An intense diet is hard to keep up for long.

examples.ko: 고강도 인터벌 운동은 시간이 짧아도 힘들어요.
examples.en: High-intensity interval training is tough even though it's short.
That factory makes high-strength steel.

examples.ko: 선수들이 고강도 훈련을 마치고 쉬고 있어요.
examples.en: The players are resting after finishing their intense training.

examples.ko: 초보자에게 고강도 운동은 무리일 수 있어요.
examples.en: High-intensity exercise can be too much for beginners.

explain: 운동, 훈련, 노동 앞에 붙여서 '고강도 운동'처럼 많이 써요. 반대말은 '저강도'예요. 힘든 정도가 센 일이나 '고강도 압박'처럼 뉴스에서 센 조치를 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is attached before words like exercise, training and labor, as in '고강도 운동'. The opposite is '저강도'. It is also used in the news for strong measures, such as '고강도 압박'.

examples.en: The bus slowly climbs the winding mountain road.
In winter, the hill road is dangerous because of the snow.
Once we get over this pass, we're at my village.
Riding a bike on a hill road leaves you out of breath.

examples.ko: 할머니는 매일 고갯길을 걸어서 시장에 가셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother walked over the hill road to the market every day.
It's my first time driving on a hill road, so I'm very nervous.

explain: '고개'는 몸의 목·머리도 뜻하지만, 산을 넘는 곳을 말할 때는 '고개를 넘다'처럼 써요. '고갯길'은 그런 길을 분명히 말할 때 쓰고, '고갯길을 오르다/내려가다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: '고개' also means the head or neck, but for a mountain pass you say '고개를 넘다'. '고갯길' makes it clear you mean the road, and it goes with '오르다' and '내려가다'.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 고급품만 팔아서 값이 비싸요.
examples.en: This shop only sells high-end goods, so it's expensive.
I'd like to buy you a high-quality item as a gift.
It's a premium product, so it doesn't break even after long use.
There's a reason premium goods cost so much.
The department store has a separate section for luxury goods.
I prefer practical things to high-end products.

explain: '명품'은 이름난 브랜드의 물건을 말할 때 많이 쓰고, '고급품'은 품질이 좋은 물건 전체에 써요. 반대로 값싸고 질이 낮은 물건은 '저가품'이나 '싸구려'라고 해요.
explain_en: '명품' is often used for famous-brand goods, while '고급품' covers any item of good quality. The opposite is '저가품' or '싸구려' for cheap, low-quality goods.

examples.en: At dawn, the fishing boats went out to sea.
Many fishing boats are gathered at the harbor.

examples.ko: 큰 파도 때문에 고기잡이배가 돌아오지 못했어요.
examples.en: The fishing boat couldn't return because of the big waves.
My father works on a small fishing boat.
As evening came, every fishing boat turned on its lights.

examples.ko: 고기잡이배를 타 보니 배가 많이 흔들려요.
examples.en: Now that I'm on a fishing boat, it rocks a lot.

explain: '고깃배'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 뉴스나 설명문에서는 한자어 '어선'을 자주 써요. '고기잡이'는 물고기를 잡는 일을 뜻해서 '고기잡이를 나가다'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: '고깃배' means the same, and news and written explanations often use the Sino-Korean '어선'. '고기잡이' is the act of fishing, as in '고기잡이를 나가다'.

examples.en: I took a lump of meat out of the freezer and thawed it.

examples.ko: 큰 고깃덩이를 먹기 좋게 썰어 주세요.
examples.en: Please cut the big chunk of meat into bite-sized pieces.
The dog ran off with a lump of meat in its mouth.
The chunks of meat in the soup were big, so it was really generous.
I bought a whole slab of meat at the mart.
The butcher put the chunk of meat on the scale.

explain: 썰지 않은 큰 고기 덩어리를 말할 때 써요. '고깃덩어리'와 같은 뜻이에요. 사람이나 몸에 빗대어 말하면 무례하게 들릴 수 있으니 조심해요.
explain_en: It refers to a big uncut piece of meat, and '고깃덩어리' means the same. Using it figuratively about a person or body can sound rude, so be careful.

examples.en: I tripped on a rock and fell flat on my face.
The child was running, tumbled forward and hurt his knee.
The stock price is suddenly plunging.

examples.ko: 자전거가 급정거하자 몸이 앞으로 고꾸라질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: When the bike stopped suddenly, I almost toppled forward.
I was so sleepy that I fell asleep as if collapsing onto my desk.
The runner took a tumble right before the finish line.

explain: '넘어지다'보다 앞으로 푹 엎어지는 느낌이 강해요. 사람이 쓰러질 때뿐 아니라 주가나 실적이 크게 떨어질 때도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '넘어지다', it strongly suggests pitching forward onto one's face. It is also used figuratively when stock prices or results drop sharply.

examples.en: There were many high-difficulty questions on this exam.
That athlete pulled off a highly difficult move.
It's an advanced dish, so it's hard for beginners.

examples.ko: 이 수학 문제집은 고난도 문제만 모아 놓았어요.
examples.en: This math workbook collects only hard problems.
They say the highly difficult surgery ended safely.

examples.ko: 처음부터 고난도 수업을 듣지 말고 쉬운 것부터 하세요.
examples.en: Don't take an advanced class from the start; begin with an easy one.

explain: '난이도가 높은'을 짧게 말한 느낌으로, 문제·기술·수술·요리 앞에 붙여 써요. 반대로 쉬울 때는 '난도가 낮은'이나 그냥 '쉬운'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a short way of saying 'high in difficulty' and goes before words like problem, technique, surgery or dish. For the opposite, say '난도가 낮은' or simply '쉬운'.

examples.en: A high-protein diet is good after working out.
Eggs are cheap and a high-protein food.
I'm on a diet, so I eat a high-protein lunch box.
If I eat only high-protein food, my stomach feels heavy.

examples.ko: 헬스장 앞 가게에서 고단백 간식을 팔아요.
examples.en: The shop in front of the gym sells high-protein snacks.

examples.ko: 이 사료는 고단백이라 강아지가 잘 커요.
examples.en: This feed is high in protein, so the puppy grows well.

explain: 식품, 식단, 간식 앞에 붙여서 많이 써요. '고단백 저지방'처럼 함께 나오는 일이 많고, 반대말은 '저단백'이에요.
explain_en: It goes before words like food, diet and snack. It often appears in the pair '고단백 저지방', and the opposite is '저단백'.

examples.en: I bought a reddish-brown leather bag.
A dark brown coat suits autumn well.
The fallen leaves turned reddish brown.

examples.ko: 이 소파는 짙은 고동색이라 때가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: This sofa is a deep brown, so dirt doesn't show much.
What socks would go well with brown shoes?
I dyed my hair a reddish brown.

explain: 갈색 중에서도 짙고 붉은 기가 도는 색을 말해요. 일상에서는 그냥 '갈색'이라고도 많이 해요. 가죽, 나무, 낙엽 같은 것의 색을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a dark brown with a reddish tint. In daily talk people often just say '갈색'. It suits describing the color of leather, wood or fallen leaves.

examples.en: Long icicles hang from the edge of the eaves.

examples.ko: 아침 햇볕에 고드름이 녹아서 물이 떨어져요.
examples.en: The icicles melt in the morning sun and water drips down.
I can hear the sound of icicles melting and trickling.
The kids snapped off icicles and played with them.
Be careful, because falling icicles are dangerous.
When winter comes, icicles form on the roof.

explain: '고드름이 달리다, 얼다, 녹다'처럼 함께 써요. 손으로 떼어 낼 때는 '고드름을 따다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '달리다', '얼다' and '녹다'. When you snap one off by hand, you say '고드름을 따다'.

examples.en: While driving at night, I saw a water deer on the road.
In the countryside, water deer come down into the fields.

examples.ko: 고라니 울음소리가 무서워서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The water deer's cry was so scary that I couldn't sleep.
A water deer jumped out in front of the car on the mountain road.
A water deer looks like a deer but has no antlers.
The farmers worry a lot because of water deer.

explain: 사슴과 비슷하게 생겼지만 다른 동물이에요. 시골길이나 논밭 이야기, 도로에서 차에 치이는 '로드킬' 뉴스에 나오기도 해요.
explain_en: It looks like a deer but is a different animal. It comes up in stories about country roads and fields, and in news about roadkill.

examples.en: A man was shouting at the top of his lungs on the street.

examples.ko: 동네가 떠나가게 고래고래 외치는 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: Someone was yelling so loudly that the whole neighborhood could hear.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 고래고래 울었어요.
examples.en: The child bawled loudly, asking me to buy a toy.

examples.ko: 옆집에서 밤새 고래고래 싸우는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: All night I heard loud shouting from the next door.

examples.ko: 고래고래 소리 지르지 말고 조용히 말해요.
examples.en: Don't yell at the top of your voice; speak quietly.

examples.ko: 축구 경기를 보며 친구가 고래고래 응원했어요.
examples.en: My friend cheered at the top of his voice while watching the soccer match.

explain: '소리를 지르다, 외치다, 울다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 화가 났거나 흥분해서 시끄럽게 내는 소리일 때가 많아서 대체로 부정적인 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It goes with verbs like '소리를 지르다', '외치다' and '울다'. It usually describes noisy shouting out of anger or excitement, so it tends to sound negative.

en: the aged; a senior citizen; an aged person

examples.ko: 버스에는 고령자를 위한 자리가 따로 있어요.
examples.en: The bus has separate seats for the elderly.

examples.ko: 고령자는 독감 예방 주사를 무료로 맞을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Seniors can get a flu shot for free.
Many elderly people live in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 고령자 일자리를 늘려야 한다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a news story saying we need more jobs for older people.

examples.ko: 고령자도 쉽게 쓸 수 있는 휴대폰이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A phone that even seniors can use easily has come out.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 고령자에게 할인을 해 줘요.
examples.en: This restaurant gives a discount to seniors.

explain: 뉴스, 제도, 안내문에서 쓰는 중립적인 말이에요. 사람에게 직접 말하거나 높여서 부를 때는 '어르신'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a neutral word used in news, policies and notices. When speaking to or about someone respectfully, say '어르신' instead.

examples.ko: 창고 문을 열자 고리타분한 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: When I opened the storeroom door, there was a musty smell.
The old blanket gives off a stale smell.
My father's way of thinking is a bit old-fashioned.
Please stop with that stuffy old talk.
It's damp inside the closet, so it smells stale.

examples.ko: 규칙이 너무 고리타분해서 아무도 안 좋아해요.
examples.en: The rules are so outdated and stuffy that nobody likes them.

explain: 냄새가 퀴퀴할 때도 쓰지만, 생각이나 방식이 낡고 답답할 때 더 많이 써요. '구식이다'나 '케케묵다'와 비슷해요. 상대방에게 직접 말하면 무례하게 들려요.
explain_en: It can describe a stale smell, but it is more often used for thinking or methods that feel outdated and stuffy. It is close to '구식이다' and '케케묵다'. Saying it directly to someone sounds rude.

examples.ko: 국수 위에 달걀 지단을 고명으로 올려요.
examples.en: I put egg strips on top of the noodles as a garnish.
For tteokguk, you top it with seaweed and meat as garnish.

examples.ko: 고명을 예쁘게 올리면 음식이 더 맛있어 보여요.
examples.en: If you arrange the garnish nicely, the food looks tastier.
I sprinkled sesame seeds on the japchae as a garnish.

examples.ko: 고명 없이 먹어도 맛있지만 있으면 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: It tastes good without garnish, but it looks nicer with it.

examples.ko: 할머니는 대추를 꽃 모양 고명으로 만드셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother made jujubes into flower-shaped garnishes.

explain: 맛보다는 모양과 색을 살리려고 음식 위에 올리는 것을 말해요. 지단, 김가루, 깨, 실고추 같은 것이 있고 '고명을 올리다/얹다'라고 써요.
explain_en: It is what you put on top of a dish, mainly to add shape and color rather than flavor. Examples are egg strips, seaweed flakes, sesame and thread chili; you say '고명을 올리다' or '얹다'.

examples.en: In summer, we rode a rubber boat in the valley.
The kids are having fun on the rubber boat.

examples.ko: 고무보트에 바람을 넣는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to pump air into the rubber boat.

examples.ko: 파도가 센 날에는 고무보트를 타면 위험해요.
examples.en: Riding a rubber boat on a day with strong waves is dangerous.
The rescue team saved people using a rubber boat.

examples.ko: 고무보트는 가벼워서 혼자서도 옮길 수 있어요.
examples.en: A rubber boat is light, so you can carry it by yourself.

explain: 사람이 안에 앉아서 타는 배라서 몸에 끼는 '튜브'와는 달라요. 바람을 넣어 쓰기 때문에 '바람을 넣다, 타다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.
explain_en: You sit inside it like a boat, so it differs from a '튜브' that you wear around your body. It is inflated, so it goes with '바람을 넣다' and '타다'.

examples.en: I always wear rubber gloves when doing dishes.
The rubber gloves tore, so I bought new ones.
My hands got rough, so I clean wearing rubber gloves.
Water got inside the rubber gloves.
Mom, where are the rubber gloves?
I made kimchi wearing red rubber gloves.

explain: '장갑을 끼다/벗다'처럼 '끼다'와 함께 써요. 설거지나 청소, 김장할 때 쓰는 두꺼운 장갑이라서 얇은 '비닐장갑'과 구분해요.
explain_en: Use it with '끼다' and '벗다', as in '장갑을 끼다'. It is a thick glove for dishes, cleaning and kimchi making, so it is distinguished from thin '비닐장갑'.

examples.en: Because of high prices, grocery shopping is scary.
These are days of high prices, so I've cut back on eating out.
With high prices and the same salary, life is hard.
The government announced measures against high prices.

examples.ko: 고물가 속에서도 싸게 사는 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for ways to buy things cheaply even amid high prices.
If high prices continue, spending will fall.

explain: 뉴스에서 '고물가, 고금리, 고환율'처럼 짝을 지어 자주 나와요. '물가가 오르다'를 짧게 말한 상태이고, 반대는 '저물가'예요.
explain_en: In the news it often appears in sets like '고물가, 고금리, 고환율'. It describes a state where '물가가 오르다', and the opposite is '저물가'.

examples.ko: 안 쓰는 철제 의자를 고물상에 팔았어요.
examples.en: I sold my unused metal chair to the junkyard.
The local junk dealer took away the scrap paper.
There are lots of old things at a junk shop.
My grandfather ran a junk business when he was young.

examples.ko: 빈 병과 캔을 모아서 고물상에 가져갔어요.
examples.en: I collected empty bottles and cans and took them to the junk dealer.

examples.ko: 고물상 앞에 고철이 산처럼 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Scrap metal is piled up like a mountain in front of the junkyard.

explain: 고철, 폐지, 빈 병처럼 못 쓰게 된 물건을 사 가는 가게나 그 일을 하는 사람을 말해요. 쓸 만한 중고 물건을 파는 중고 가게와는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: It is a shop, or the person running it, that buys scrap metal, waste paper and empty bottles. It differs from a secondhand store that sells usable goods.

examples.ko: 회사의 비리를 알린 고발자가 보호를 받고 있어요.
examples.en: The whistle-blower who exposed the company's corruption is being protected.
The name of the whistle-blower was not made public.
He found courage and became a whistle-blower.
They say we need a law that protects whistle-blowers.
The accuser's and the accused's stories are different.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 나온 고발자가 직접 기자회견을 했어요.
examples.en: The whistle-blower from the news held a press conference in person.

explain: 회사나 조직 안의 잘못을 알리는 사람은 '내부 고발자'라고 해요. 법에서는 피해자가 직접 하면 '고소', 제3자도 할 수 있는 신고를 '고발'이라고 구분해요.
explain_en: Someone who exposes wrongdoing inside a company or organization is called an '내부 고발자'. In law, a victim filing is '고소', while '고발' is a report that a third party can also make.

examples.ko: 이 일을 맡으면 고생길이 열릴 것 같아요.
examples.en: If I take on this job, hard times seem to be coming.
As soon as I joined the new company, the hardship began.
They say that raising a child is a road of hardship.

examples.ko: 그 먼 곳까지 걸어가다니 고생길이 따로 없네요.
examples.en: Walking all the way to that far place is real hardship.
I feel sorry for my son, who has started down a hard road.
I started a business for no good reason and ended up on a road of hardship.

explain: 고생을 길에 빗대어 '고생길이 열리다, 고생길로 접어들다, 고생길에 들어서다'처럼 써요. 고생이 길게 이어질 것 같은 상황에서 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 이렇게 일이 많으면 앞으로 고생길이 훤해요.
phrases.en: With this much work, hard times are clearly ahead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 고생이 많을 것이 뻔히 보일 때 써요. 걱정하거나 농담처럼 말할 때 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is obvious that tough times lie ahead; often said with worry or as a joke.

explain_en: It likens hardship to a road, as in '고생길이 열리다', '고생길로 접어들다' and '고생길에 들어서다'. People use it when the hardship seems likely to continue for a long time.

en: future trouble; trouble in the future

examples.en: People say that once you marry, hard times begin.
For new employees, hard times begin as soon as they join.
Once I started packing for the move, the hard work began.

examples.ko: 이번 프로젝트는 시작부터 고생문이 열린 느낌이에요.
examples.en: This project feels like trouble from the very start.

examples.ko: 고생문에 들어선 친구에게 힘내라고 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: I told my friend, who has entered a hard stretch, to hang in there.

examples.ko: 아이가 태어나면 고생문이 열린다는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that when a baby is born, the hardship begins.

explain: 앞으로 닥칠 고생을 문에 빗대어 '고생문이 열리다'처럼 거의 이 짝으로 써요. 걱정스럽거나 농담 섞인 말투로 말할 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: If twins are born, you can see the hard times ahead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 힘든 일이 많을 것이 뻔할 때 써요. 놀리듯이 말할 때도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is plain that a lot of hardship lies ahead; sometimes said teasingly.

explain_en: It pictures upcoming hardship as a door, and is used almost always as '고생문이 열리다'. It is often said in a worried or joking tone.

en: someone preparing to take a state exam

examples.ko: 제 동생은 공무원 시험을 준비하는 고시생이에요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is an exam candidate preparing for the civil service test.
Exam candidates study at the library until late at night.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 고시생을 위한 작은 방이 많아요.
examples.en: This neighborhood has many small rooms for exam candidates.

examples.ko: 고시생 때는 친구를 거의 못 만났어요.
examples.en: When I was an exam candidate, I hardly met friends.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 고시생에게 밥값을 깎아 줘요.
examples.en: This restaurant gives exam candidates a discount.

examples.ko: 오랜 시간 고시생으로 지내서 많이 지쳤어요.
examples.en: I spent a long time as an exam candidate and got very worn out.

explain: 나라에서 보는 큰 시험을 준비하는 사람을 말해요. 요즘은 공무원 시험을 준비하는 사람을 '공시생'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a person preparing for a major state-run exam. These days, someone preparing for the civil service exam is also called a '공시생'.

examples.en: These earphones play music in high sound quality.
High-quality audio files are large.

examples.ko: 고음질 스피커를 사고 싶은데 너무 비싸요.
examples.en: I want to buy a high-fidelity speaker, but it's too expensive.
I turned on the high-quality setting in the streaming app.

examples.ko: 영상은 화질이 중요하지만 음악은 고음질이 중요해요.
examples.en: For videos picture quality matters, but for music high sound quality matters.
It was recorded in high quality, so the sound is very clean.

explain: '고화질'과 짝을 이루는 말로, 음원·이어폰·스피커 앞에 붙어요. 높은 소리를 뜻하는 '고음'과 헷갈리기 쉽지만 소리가 높다는 뜻이 아니에요. 음악 앱에서 '고음질 재생'을 켜면 소리는 좋아지는 대신 데이터를 더 써요.
explain_en: It pairs with '고화질' and goes before words like music files, earphones and speakers. It is easy to confuse with '고음' (high pitch), but it does not mean a high-pitched sound. Turning on 'high-quality playback' in a music app improves the sound but uses more data.

examples.en: That foul looked deliberate.

examples.ko: 늦은 건 고의적이 아니라 길이 막혀서예요.
examples.en: I wasn't late on purpose; the road was blocked.
A deliberate mistake is hard to forgive.

examples.ko: 고의적 방해 행위는 처벌받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Deliberate acts of obstruction can be punished.

examples.ko: 옆 사람이 고의적으로 부딪친 것 같아서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I got angry because it seemed the person next to me bumped into me on purpose.
I didn't lie on purpose.

explain: 일상에서는 '일부러'를 많이 쓰고, '고의적'은 뉴스나 법, 격식 있는 말에서 자주 써요. 반대는 '우발적'이나 '과실'이고, '고의적인, 고의적으로' 꼴로 써요.
explain_en: In daily speech people say '일부러' more, while '고의적' appears in news, law and formal speech. The opposites are '우발적' and '과실', and it is used as '고의적인' or '고의적으로'.

examples.en: My younger sibling tattled on me to Mom.
Because of the snitching, the friends drifted apart.
Please don't go telling on me to the teacher.

examples.ko: 이건 고자질이 아니라 꼭 알려야 하는 일이에요.
examples.en: This isn't tattling; it's something that must be reported.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 고자질을 많이 해서 혼났어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I got scolded for tattling a lot.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 고자질을 잘해서 인기가 없어요.
examples.en: That friend tattles a lot, so he's not popular.

explain: 남의 잘못을 윗사람에게 몰래 말하는 나쁜 느낌의 말이라서 주로 아이들 사이에서 많이 나와요. 꼭 알려야 하는 일은 '신고'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: It has a negative tone, and is heard a lot among children. When something truly must be reported, people use '신고' instead.

examples.ko: 동생이 제가 몰래 과자를 먹었다고 고자질했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling told on me for secretly eating snacks.
A friend tattled to the teacher, so I got scolded.
Don't snitch; I'll tell them myself.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 다른 친구들 잘못을 자주 고자질해요.
examples.en: That child often tattles on other kids' mistakes.
I still don't know who snitched.
I'm worried my older brother will tell on me to Dad.

explain: '누구에게 고자질하다'처럼 '한테/에게/께'와 함께 써요. 비슷한 말로 '일러바치다'가 있는데 아이들 말에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It takes '한테', '에게' or '께' for the person told, as in '누구에게 고자질하다'. A similar word is '일러바치다', often heard in kids' speech.

examples.ko: 한국에 온 지 고작해야 일주일밖에 안 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been barely a week since I came to Korea.

examples.ko: 이 식당 점심은 고작해야 팔천 원이에요.
examples.en: Lunch at this restaurant is eight thousand won at most.

examples.ko: 오늘 온 사람은 고작해야 열 명 정도예요.
examples.en: The people who came today are about ten at best.
My salary is, at best, about enough for living expenses.

examples.ko: 고작해야 한두 번 만난 사이인데 너무 친한 척하네요.
examples.en: We've met only once or twice at most, yet he acts so close.

examples.ko: 고작해야 숙제 하나 때문에 그렇게 화를 내요?
examples.en: You're that angry over just one piece of homework?

explain: 수나 양이 적다고 얕잡아 보는 느낌이 있고, 뒤에 '밖에 안', '정도' 같은 말이 자주 와요. '기껏해야'와 거의 바꿔 쓸 수 있고, 짧게 '고작'만 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It carries a sense of looking down on a small amount, and often comes with '밖에 안' or '정도'. It can almost always be swapped with '기껏해야', and sometimes the short '고작' is used.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 고전적인 사랑 이야기를 다뤄요.
examples.en: This movie deals with a classic love story.
It's an old-fashioned method, but it definitely works.

examples.ko: 그 카페는 고전적 분위기로 꾸며져 있어요.
examples.en: That cafe is decorated with a classical atmosphere.
I got fooled again by a classic trick.
I like watches with a classic design.
Your outfit is so old-style that it stands out.

explain: '클래식한' 같은 좋은 뜻으로도, '낡은 방식'이라는 나쁜 뜻으로도 쓰여서 앞뒤 말을 보고 판단해요. '전통적'은 이어져 내려온 것을, '고전적'은 오래된 틀이나 방식 그대로인 것을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It can be positive like 'classic' or negative like 'outdated', so judge from the context. '전통적' stresses what has been passed down, while '고전적' suits an old form or way kept as it is.

examples.en: I don't have a regular income yet.
The shop is stable because it has regular customers.

examples.ko: 고정적 지출을 줄이면 돈을 모을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you cut fixed expenses, you can save money.
Set a regular time for exercising.
My job isn't steady, so getting a loan is hard.

examples.ko: 이 모임은 고정적인 멤버 없이 자유롭게 와요.
examples.en: In this group, people come freely without set members.

explain: '고정적인 수입, 직장, 손님'처럼 늘 일정하게 이어지는 것에 써요. 반대말은 '유동적'이에요. 움직이지 않게 붙어 있는 상태를 말하는 '고정된'과는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: It goes with things that stay steady, such as '고정적인 수입', '직장' and '손님'. The opposite is '유동적'. It differs from '고정된', which describes something held in place.
